summary: Tested the 4-item owner batch end to end, backend and frontend. Working: FIX 1 receivables (API and System Wallet UI), FIX 1b Excel ties to the API for cashback, FIX 2 withdrawal collects the cashback owed first, FIX 3 refund math for a single line (₹4,500 paid by the seller, treasury untouched, replaying it pays nothing), FIX 4/4b service reviews and visit charges, and the frontend provider card and apply screen. Found 1 CRITICAL bug: the SECOND partial return on the same order pays nothing and nets nothing, yet the refund call reports success. Also found an Excel Receivables mismatch, verified with a parked return_refund row. All regression suites pass. One of them (test_iter96) wrote vendor_earnings directly and knocked testvendor's ledger ₹6,000 out of sync. I reverted that write and fixed the test. vendor_wallet_view(VID) is now in_sync=True with unledgered_difference=0.

critical.issue: The second (and any later) partial return on the SAME order pays nothing and nets nothing, but process_refund still reports success with the gross refund_amount. Root cause: the transactions unique index uniq_user_type_order (user_id, type, order_id), created in server.py:7618, rejects a second row of each of these types for the same order: cashback_netted_off_refund (customer), return_refund_debit (seller) and return_refund_credit (customer). core/shop_money.py:139-143 swallows ANY E11000 and returns None, so no money moves and no error is raised. Reproduction: tests/test_iter102_partial_return_netting.py. Return 1 is correct (₹2,700 paid, ₹300 netted). Return 2 nets 0, the customer gets +0 and the seller pays 0, yet refund_amount reports 2000. A financial_errors row 'return_cashback_reversal_failed E11000' is written. Return 3 behaves the same.

minor.issue: The 'Other advances' section counts every open vendor_outstanding row whose kind is not cashback (wallet_export.py:433-445). The API's vendor_receivable counts only return_refund_company_funded, delivery_fee_company_funded and delivery_fee (finance.py:399-403). A parked return_refund row therefore shows in Excel but not on screen. Verified: API 0 vs Excel 120. The Excel 'RECEIVABLES TOTAL' also leaves out pending_collections, which the API's receivables_total includes. It is currently 0, so the totals only match by chance.

Updating reversed_total on cashback_ledger is a read-then-write, not atomic (cashback.py:614-667). Two concurrent refunds could both net the same cashback. Use a conditional update ({_id, reversed_total: already}) or $inc with a guard.

If reverse_partial_cashback raises, the return is still marked cashback_status='handled' with netted=0 and the FULL gross is paid (returns.py:527-539). The customer keeps the cashback AND gets the full refund, and the only trace is a financial_errors row.

Each seller-to-customer return refund makes the legacy checker book a 'legacy_reconcile_inflow' audit row on the admin. ₹4,500 and ₹2,700 were booked today from the refund tests. The checker treats return_refund_credit into user wallets as phantom inflow. These rows are audit-only (admin buckets did not move), but they work against the 'every rupee trackable' goal.

The authorisation check is is_service_provider OR service_status=='approved' (service_provider.py:89). A suspended or rejected provider who still has is_service_provider=True can edit his listing and visit charge.

ui_bugs.issue: The placeholder says 'leave empty for “On request”', but an empty field sends visit_charge: undefined (apply.tsx:193), so the old charge stays. Only typing 0 resets it.
The touch target is 26px tall, below the 44px minimum.

issues: Negative net worth shows as '₹-37,185.34'. It should read '−₹37,185.34'.

The '· Cashback owed by sellers' and '· Refunds / fees' tiles are styled as peers of '+ Receivables'. Visually this can read as being added twice. Consider indenting or nesting them under Receivables.
The 'How it works' copy says '₹0.00 (₹0.00 fee + 18% GST)' while the checkbox right below says 'customer pays ₹1'. The two contradict each other.
On web, Alert.alert is a no-op, so there is no 'Saved' confirmation (the edit mode just closes).
Legacy listings with no category_id or languages cannot save a visit charge alone. Validation forces the provider to re-pick both first.
Feather 'star' is outline-only, so a 5.0 rating never looks filled.

action_items: CRITICAL: fix multi-partial-return refunds. Narrow or replace the uniq_user_type_order index so it does not cover rows already protected by idempotency_key (for example, exclude the return_refund_debit, return_refund_credit and cashback_netted_off_refund types, or move per-return rows to a return-scoped key). ALSO make shop_money._insert return None ONLY when the duplicate is on idempotency_key, and raise for any other unique index. Then make process_refund confirm both money rows were written before setting refund_status='paid'. Re-run tests/test_iter102_partial_return_netting.py, which should pass 21/21.

Excel Receivables sheet: use the same kind filter as finance.py (return_refund_company_funded, delivery_fee_company_funded, delivery_fee), and add pending_collections to 'RECEIVABLES TOTAL', so Excel always equals master.receivables_total.
apply.tsx: send visit_charge: 0 when the field is cleared, to match the 'leave empty for On request' placeholder.
reverse_partial_cashback: make the reversed_total update atomic. process_refund: do not pay the full gross when netting raised an error (park or retry instead).
Optional: teach the legacy money-flow checker that return_refund_credit is a transfer out of vendor_earnings, so it stops booking legacy_reconcile_inflow rows.
Optional UI polish: make the Write review button at least 44px tall, format negative net worth as −₹, use singular 'review', and fix the reveal-fee copy.
critical_code_review_comments: core/shop_money.py:139-143 treats ANY duplicate-key error as an idempotent replay. Combined with the legacy uniq_user_type_order index, this silently drops real money rows, which is the root cause of the critical bug.

FIX 2 withdrawal ledger is clean: exactly one row each of CBRECOVER-WDL, WDLFEE, WDLFEEREV and WDL. On reject, WDL_REJECT, WDL_FEEBACK and WDLFEEREV_REJECT are written and the cashback recovery stays collected (correct).

FIX 1: cashback_receivable comes from users.cashback_outstanding and the open cashback rows are excluded from vendor_receivable, so there is no double count. A ₹350 seed added exactly 350 to receivables_total and net_worth, and no other Excel sheet repeated it.
server.py (10,892 lines), finance.py (1,376), returns.py (800) and cashback.py (964) are all over the 700-line guideline.

The services_and_withdrawal test funds the wallet to ₹6,000 and unfunds it afterwards, but its seeded ₹300 cashback outstanding is genuinely collected into the treasury on every run. test_iter96 settlement now SKIPS when the wallet is under ₹5,200; fund it via shop_money.credit first. rca_of_issue: FIX 3b: the transactions unique index uniq_user_type_order(user_id, type, order_id) means each (user, type, order) can appear only once. Return #2 on the same order tries to insert a second cashback_netted_off_refund, return_refund_debit and return_refund_credit row for that order. The memo insert raises E11000, which is caught as a cashback failure, so netted=0. shop_money._insert then swallows E11000 for the debit and credit and returns None. process_refund carries on and marks the return paid, with no balance change. Mitigation: scope the legacy index away from idempotency-keyed rows, and only treat an idempotency_key collision as a replay.
